title: Bayesian Attribution of Cell-Based Bioelectric Biosensor Responses to D1- and D2-Like Dopamine Receptors: A Standalone Predictive Tool
content: Cell-based bioelectric biosensors report the membrane-potential response of a whole cultured cell population within minutes, but the recorded trace is a lumped signal that does not indicate which receptor population produced it. Starting from a Bioelectric Recognition Assay (BERA) in which N2a mouse neuroblastoma cells depolarize at nanomolar and hyperpolarize at micromolar dopamine concentrations, we developed a predictive tool that converts such recordings into posterior probabilities over the receptor arms responsible. The response is modelled as the sum of a depolarizing D1-like arm and a hyperpolarizing D2-like arm, each a Hill function of dopamine concentration; eticlopride enters as a competitive shift of both arms plus a term for relief of tonic D2 tone, and sodium ions as a scaling of D2-like efficacy and affinity. Four hypotheses (D1-like only, D2-like only, both, neither) are compared by marginal likelihood. The tool assigns the nanomolar response to D1-like receptors (P = 0.89), the micromolar response to D2-like receptors (P = 1.00) and the sodium-shifted response to a weakened D2-like arm (P = 0.97), while flagging the eticlopride-only series as unidentifiable for the D1 arm. On synthetic data at the reproducibility of the assay, the correct hypothesis is recovered in every replicate, and a minor second arm is detected once its gain reaches one fifth of the dominant one. A paired ± eticlopride module returns P = 0.96 for D2-like agonism by 10% Vitex agnus-castus immature-fruit extract. The tool is a single 28 kB HTML file that runs offline in any browser.
